title: Missing Logout/Session Termination Endpoint
description:
The application lacks a logout functionality to properly terminate user sessions. There is no /logout endpoint or session termination mechanism implemented. This means:

1. Users cannot manually terminate their sessions
2. Session cookies remain valid indefinitely (only expire based on browser behavior)
3. Combined with missing HttpOnly flag on cookies, stolen cookies remain useful forever
4. No server-side session invalidation is possible
5. Users on shared computers cannot ensure their session is terminated after use

Common logout endpoints (/logout, /exit, /signout, /logoff, /user/logout, /auth/logout) all return HTTP 404 Not Found responses, indicating no logout functionality exists in the application.
impact:
Without proper logout functionality:
- Users cannot ensure their session is terminated after use (critical for shared computers)
- On shared computers, the next user could access the previous user's bookmarks and session
- Stolen session cookies remain valid indefinitely, extending the window of opportunity for attackers
- Increases risk from session fixation and hijacking attacks significantly
- When combined with missing HttpOnly and Secure flags on cookies, provides attackers with multiple attack vectors
- Violates OWASP A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures
- Violates OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control in shared environment scenarios
evidence:
POC execution results demonstrate:

1. All common logout endpoints return HTTP 404:
   - /logout: HTTP 404
   - /exit: HTTP 404
   - /signout: HTTP 404
   - /logoff: HTTP 404
   - /user/logout: HTTP 404
   - /auth/logout: HTTP 404

2. Session persistence verified:
   - POST /login establishes session cookie
   - GET /list with session cookie: HTTP 200 (session valid)
   - GET /list after delay: HTTP 200 (session still valid after time passes)
   - POST /logout attempt: HTTP 404 (no endpoint exists)
   - GET /list after logout attempt: HTTP 200 (session cannot be terminated)

3. Confirmed behaviors:
   - No logout endpoint exists
   - Session cookies cannot be manually terminated by users
   - Sessions persist indefinitely
   - No server-side session invalidation mechanism is implemented
remediation:
1. Implement a /logout endpoint (or /signout, /exit - choose one standard path) that:
   - Clears session cookies by setting them with Max-Age=0 or Expires in the past
   - Invalidates the session server-side if sessions are stored (recommended)
   - Redirects to login page or home page after successful logout
   - Returns HTTP 302 or 303 redirect status

2. Add logout button/link in the application UI:
   - Include in navigation bar/menu
   - Make easily accessible to all authenticated users
   - Ensure it triggers the logout endpoint

3. Implement session timeout mechanisms:
   - Set session expiration (e.g., 30 minutes of inactivity)
   - Implement absolute session timeout (e.g., 8 hours maximum)
   - Invalidate session server-side when timeout is reached
   - Notify user before timeout occurs if possible

4. Implement additional session management controls:
   - Invalidate all existing sessions when user changes password
   - Provide option for user to terminate all active sessions from account settings
   - Implement server-side session store to track active sessions
   - Add session IDs instead of relying solely on cookies

5. Set appropriate HTTP headers to prevent caching of authenticated pages:
   - Cache-Control: private, no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate
   - Pragma: no-cache
   - Expires: 0 or past date

6. Set secure cookie attributes:
   - HttpOnly flag to prevent JavaScript access
   - Secure flag to enforce HTTPS-only transmission
   - SameSite=Strict to prevent CSRF attacks
references: OWASP A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures, OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, CWE-384: Session Fixation, CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration, OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet
